around.headline: Eicher vehicle rams private travel bus on Hyderabad-Bengaluru route, 10 critical
around.summary: An Eicher vehicle collided with a Hyderabad-Bengaluru private travel bus overnight, leaving 10 passengers in critical condition — a separate incident from this morning's Bengaluru-Mysuru bus crash, making it a rough weekend for intercity travel on both corridors. If you're on an overnight or early-morning intercity bus this weekend, pick an operator with a recent safety record and avoid the front-most seats where possible.

around.headline: Namma Metro gets CBTC signalling approval and ₹26,447 crore from the Centre
around.summary: The Railway Board has cleared CBTC (Communication-Based Train Control) signalling for the Pink and Blue metro lines, and the Centre has released ₹26,447 crore in funding — both steps toward more frequent trains, though today also saw a 2-hour Purple Line suspension and a Green Line technical glitch. Expect the usual mix of long-term progress and short-term hiccups on your commute for now.
around.source: The New Indian Express, Times of India, Udayavani

around.headline: Kumaraswamy tells Karnataka govt: stop collecting toll on NICE Road
around.summary: Union Minister HD Kumaraswamy has cited a High Court judgment to urge NICE Road users not to pay toll, giving the state government a 10-day deadline to act. If you regularly use NICE Road to bypass city traffic, this dispute is worth tracking before you decide whether to keep paying at the booth.
around.source: The Economic Times, India Today, Moneycontrol

around.headline: Karnataka starts footpath clearance drive for pedestrian safety
around.summary: Authorities have launched a drive to clear encroached footpaths across Bengaluru to improve pedestrian safety. If your usual walking route has vendors or parked vehicles blocking the footpath, this is the drive to flag it to.

around.headline: Jefferies drops HDFC Bank, adds MCX in its India portfolio
around.summary: Global brokerage Jefferies has removed HDFC Bank and added MCX to its recommended India portfolio, part of a wider set of changes. If you follow brokerage-driven stock moves, this is a signal worth a second look rather than an instruction to act on immediately.

around.headline: Netanyahu rejects Trump's Gaza peace plan, rules out Palestinian statehood
around.summary: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu said there will be no Palestinian state as long as he is in office, rejecting the peace plan proposed by the US, as the West Asia conflict continues. A prolonged conflict keeps global oil-price and market volatility risk elevated, which eventually shows up in fuel and import costs here too.

street_smart.title: You're out on a late-night delivery (or just walking home) when a group of strangers stops you, abuses you over the language you speak, and starts beating you with a stick. What do you do first?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real Bengaluru incident: a delivery agent was thrashed with a wooden stick by a group in Yelahanka New Town who allegedly abused him for not speaking Hindi; police registered a case and arrested four people within a day (The Hindu, India Today, The New Indian Express).
street_smart.situation: A group of strangers surrounds you over a language dispute and turns violent, hitting you with a stick before anyone else intervenes.

choices.text: Stand your ground and argue back to explain yourself and defuse things verbally.
choices.feedback: Risky. Arguing with a group that has already turned physical rarely de-escalates it — it more often gives them a reason to keep going, and you lose the seconds you need to get to safety.

choices.text: Get to safety first, call 112 immediately, then file a police complaint with photos of your injuries and any details you noticed (faces, vehicle, location).
choices.feedback: Correct. 112 dispatches the nearest police unit regardless of which station's jurisdiction you're in, and it's exactly this kind of fast complaint plus evidence that let police identify and arrest four people within a day in today's case. Getting away from the group is priority one — you can't reason with people who are already hitting you.

choices.text: Film the confrontation and post it on social media immediately, naming the attackers before going to the police.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Public shaming feels like justice, but posting unverified accusations before an FIR is filed can expose you to a defamation claim, can tip off the attackers to flee before police act, and does nothing to actually get you medical help or an official record of the assault.

choices.text: Call your delivery platform's support line first and wait for them to advise you.
choices.feedback: Risky. Platform support can log an incident and may help later, but it has no power to stop an ongoing physical assault — calling 112 first gets an actual police response to where you are.

takeaways: Dial 112 for any assault in progress — it routes to the nearest available police unit regardless of local jurisdiction, faster than looking up a specific station's number.
Photograph injuries and note down any identifying details (faces, clothing, vehicle numbers) as soon as you're safe — this is the evidence that actually gets an FIR registered and arrests made.
Don't post accusations publicly before filing a police complaint — it can boomerang into a defamation risk for you and can let attackers flee before they're identified.

quiz.question: The Railway Board this week approved which signalling system for Namma Metro's Pink and Blue lines?
quiz.why: CBTC lets trains communicate continuously with track systems, allowing them to run safely closer together — the key to running more trains per hour without new tracks.

quiz.question: Union Minister HD Kumaraswamy gave the Karnataka government how many days to act on a High Court judgment about NICE Road tolls?
quiz.why: NICE Road is a privately built and tolled corridor many commuters use to bypass Bengaluru's core traffic, which is why a dispute over its toll terms draws this much attention.

quiz.question: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu rejected a Gaza peace plan proposed by which country, saying there will be no Palestinian state as long as he's in office?
quiz.why: A prolonged West Asia conflict tends to keep global oil prices and shipping-insurance costs elevated, which eventually feeds through to fuel prices in India too.

quiz.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty?
quiz.why: Courts have interpreted Article 21 expansively over the decades to cover things well beyond its original text, including the right to a clean environment, privacy, and a speedy trial.

quiz.question: In Reserve Bank of India policy, what does the 'repo rate' refer to?
options: The rate at which RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks
The interest rate banks pay you on a savings account
The tax rate on repossessed property
quiz.why: When RBI cuts the repo rate, banks' own borrowing gets cheaper, which usually (with a lag) flows through to lower loan EMIs for consumers.
